deep.reconstruction:
Context: the bundle 'R.ElektrCyl' belongs to Riemann's posthumous work on the electrostatic equilibrium of charge on infinitely long conducting cylinders with circular cross-section and parallel axes. This reduces to a 2D potential problem in the plane exterior to several circles. This page holds the working notes for the triply connected case.

(0) Figure. Three circles with centres p, p1, p2 are drawn. Two cuts K1 (circle p to circle p1) and K2 (circle p to circle p2) join them, plus a struck-through link between p1 and p2. The cuts make the triply connected region simply connected. Labels: z=p, z=p1, z=p2.

(1) Parametrising a boundary circle. The circle about p is |z-p| = r ('mod(z-p) = r'). Points on it are written z - p = r e^{psi i}. Fix two points r e^{alpha i} and r e^{beta i} on it. Riemann considers the Möbius quotient
 Q(z) = (z - p - r e^{beta i}) / (z - p - r e^{alpha i}).
He also notes the companion expression z - p - r e^{alpha i} = r(e^{psi i} - e^{alpha i}) on the circle, and jots 1/(z-p) as the elementary singular term.

On the circle (my fill-in): e^{psi i} - e^{beta i} = 2i sin((psi-beta)/2) e^{i(psi+beta)/2}. Hence
 Q = [sin((psi-beta)/2) / sin((psi-alpha)/2)] e^{i(beta-alpha)/2}.
So e^{(alpha-beta)i/2} Q is real on the whole circle. This is the inscribed-angle theorem. It is why the factor e^{((alpha-beta)/2) i} is written in front of the bracket.

Consequently w = log(e^{(alpha-beta)i/2} Q) = g + h i (with w = u + v i in the general notation) has imaginary part 0 (mod pi) on that circle. Such functions are the building blocks for analytic functions with real values (vanishing imaginary part) on the boundary circles.

(2) Boundary-value problem stated in words. 'Imaginärer Theil gleich 0' on the boundary, 'stetig' (continuous), and
 v_xx + v_yy = 0.
The conjugate is recovered from du = (dv/dy) dx - (dv/dx) dy, which is the Cauchy-Riemann relation u_x = v_y, u_y = -v_x. To the right: 'unendlich ... allenthalben', presumably the condition on where the function may become infinite.

(3) Variational formulation. The Dirichlet-type integral
 ∫∫ [ (g_x ∓ v_y)^2 + (g_y ± v_x)^2 ] dx dy
measures the deviation of g + v i from satisfying Cauchy-Riemann. This is Riemann's Dirichlet-principle route to the existence of an analytic function with prescribed real (or imaginary) part.

(4) Killing the periods. Three such functions w, w', w'' each have moduli of periodicity (jumps across the cuts) K1, K2; K1', K2'; K1'', K2''. Form
 g = alpha w + beta w' + w''
and choose the real constants alpha, beta so that g is single-valued:
 alpha K1 + beta K1' + K1'' = 0,
 alpha K2 + beta K2' + K2'' = 0.
This is a 2x2 linear system. My fill-in: with D = K1 K2' - K1' K2,
 alpha = (K1' K2'' - K1'' K2')/D,
 beta = (K1'' K2 - K1 K2'')/D.
Two conditions correspond to the two independent cycles of a triply connected region. Physically this fixes the charges/potentials on the three cylinders.

(5) Bottom sketches. Semicircular arcs standing on a straight line, with marked segments. These are probably half-plane configurations: cylinders over a conducting plane, or images under reflection/the Möbius map. They are not worked further.
errors: In the Dirichlet integral the signs are hard to read and partly overwritten. The correct defect functional for g + v i to be analytic is (g_x - v_y)^2 + (g_y + v_x)^2. If both brackets carry '+', one sign is a slip or the conjugate is taken with opposite orientation.
The parametrization line 'z - p = ... e^{psi i}' has the factor r struck/overwritten; the intended statement is z - p = r e^{psi i}.
The solvability of the period system requires D = K1 K2' - K1' K2 ≠ 0. This is not stated; it is implicitly assumed, and it holds by linear independence of the elementary functions.

The imaginary part of log(e^{(alpha-beta)i/2} Q) on the circle is 0 only modulo pi: it jumps by pi between the arcs separated by e^{alpha i} and e^{beta i}. Riemann's 'Imaginärer Theil gleich 0' should be read with that caveat (or as applying to Q itself being real).

results.what: On the circle |z-p|=r, e^{(alpha-beta)i/2}(z-p-re^{beta i})/(z-p-re^{alpha i}) is real (constant argument of the Möbius quotient, inscribed angle theorem)
results.modern_name: Möbius transformation mapping a circle to a line / inscribed angle theorem

results.what: Harmonic conjugate via du = v_y dx - v_x dy for continuous harmonic v
Existence of the analytic function via minimizing ∫∫((g_x - v_y)^2 + (g_y + v_x)^2)
results.modern_name: Dirichlet principle (Riemann's form from the 1851 dissertation)

results.what: Making a function on a triply connected domain single-valued by a linear combination alpha w + beta w' + w'' whose periods across the two cuts vanish
results.modern_name: Elimination of periods / normalization of abelian-type integrals on multiply connected domains
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen 1857); for circular domains Schottky 1877

results.what: Electrostatics of parallel circular cylinders as a potential problem in a multiply connected plane region bounded by circles
results.modern_name: Potential theory in circle domains (precursor of Schottky's treatment of circular domains)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann's Nachlass 'Gleichgewicht der Electricität auf Cylindern mit kreisförmigem Querschnitt und parallelen Axen' (published in Werke 1876); Schottky 1877

deep.surprise_reason: These are working notes for Riemann's known Nachlass piece on electric equilibrium on parallel circular cylinders, already published in his Werke. The methods (Möbius quotient real on a circle, Cauchy-Riemann conjugate, Dirichlet principle, cancelling periods across cuts) are his standard toolkit and are well documented.

checkable.asserts: On z-p=r e^{i psi}, e^{(alpha-beta)i/2}(z-p-re^{beta i})/(z-p-re^{alpha i}) equals the real number sin((psi-beta)/2)/sin((psi-alpha)/2)
Factorization e^{i psi}-e^{i alpha} = 2i sin((psi-alpha)/2) e^{i(psi+alpha)/2}, used for r(e^{psi i}-e^{alpha i})

checkable.sympy: a,b,K1,K2,K1p,K2p,K1pp,K2pp=symbols('a b K1 K2 K1p K2p K1pp K2pp'); sol=solve([a*K1+b*K1p+K1pp, a*K2+b*K2p+K2pp],[a,b]); simplify(sol[a]-(K1p*K2pp-K1pp*K2p)/(K1*K2p-K1p*K2))==0 and simplify(sol[b]-(K1pp*K2-K1*K2pp)/(K1*K2p-K1p*K2))==0
checkable.asserts: Cramer solution of the period-cancelling system alpha K1+beta K1'+K1''=0, alpha K2+beta K2'+K2''=0

checkable.sympy: x,y=symbols('x y',real=True); w=log(x+I*y-1); u=re(expand_complex(w)); v=im(expand_complex(w)); simplify(diff(u,x)-diff(v,y))==0 and simplify(diff(u,y)+diff(v,x))==0
checkable.asserts: For analytic w=u+iv, du = v_y dx - v_x dy (Cauchy-Riemann), as written on the page
The imaginary part of the logarithmic building block is harmonic: v_xx+v_yy=0

transcription_corrections: 'e^{\frac{x-\beta}{?}i}' should read e^{\frac{\alpha-\beta}{2}i}, the phase factor making the Möbius quotient real on the circle.
The fraction in the middle is (z-p-re^{beta i})/(z-p-re^{alpha i}). The '+' in the denominator of the machine transcription is a misreading of '-', consistent with the top-right formula.
'[-...-] re^{psi i}' to the right of g+hi is a crossed-out/overwritten r e^{psi i}, i.e. the substitution z-p = r e^{psi i}.
'z-p=[-...-] r e^{psi i}' is the parametrization z - p = r e^{psi i} with overwriting.
'\frac{\partial K}{\partial x}' at the end of the integral line is uncertain. It is more likely a struck-out/overwritten derivative, and the integral ends with dx dy.
'überzugend [?] allenthalben [?]' is uncertain. Possibly 'unendlich ... überall ... allenthalben stetig', a condition on infinities/continuity; it cannot be confirmed.
'A_1 [?]' under g = alpha w + beta w' + w'' is a struck-out stray mark.
The bottom of the page contains sketches of semicircular arcs on a straight baseline (two rows) not mentioned in the transcription.
The figure, three circles with centres p, p1, p2 joined by cuts K1, K2, is not mentioned in the transcription. A struck label sits on the p1-p2 link.
